title: Louisiana state LPs and the shortage of surviving musicians
summary: Rose describes the LPs he produces for the state's Department of Commerce and Industry and the lack of replacements, especially clarinet, drums and piano.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: And I believe you were on a session with us when we did that lakefront lounger session at WTPS and we made the Pontchartrain the Beautiful and Spanish capital, you know, old Spanish fortissimo. And of course the records that I make for the state of Louisiana, which are made for the Department of Commerce and Industry, we've made now three LPs there, the third of which will be out within the next few weeks. And we're now planning to do a series of four LPs for the same purpose, except that these will go in the safe to be released as required, but as kind of insurance based on the fact that there are not as many musicians around anymore and that we can't depend on their survival long enough to wait for years in order to record them.
Well, there aren't any replacements. Unfortunately that's the case. We're especially weak in piano and drums and clarinet.

Well we can still manage with trombone and cornet though. There are still some trombone and cornet players. But clarinet players who can play the harmonic role of a clarinet in a jazz band, we don't have. As you recall we found that Eddie Miller was in shape to play clarinet last time, and he hadn't played in thirty years, but he broke out his clarinet and we did make a session. And I don't know what we're going to do exactly next time. I have some plans, enough to cut four more sessions. But we only have the two drummers that are really up to the kind of musical standard that is useful for us now in Sae and Louis Barberan. And we have, of course, Armand Hug and Jeanette Kimball who can play the piano for these purposes, possibly Jeff Riddick. And if Stanley Mendelsohn is in shape we could use him too. And I would like nothing better on this series of four if we could use all four piano players,
